questions.q: Which field on the `change_request` table holds Standard, Normal, or Emergency?
options: The `type` field
The `state` field
The `category` field
The `risk` field
questions.explain: The `type` field on `change_request` is set to Standard, Normal, or Emergency, and drives which workflow path the change follows.

questions.q: Why can a Standard change move toward implementation without an individual approval record?
options: Because approvals are disabled platform-wide for all changes
Because it's created from a pre-approved Change Template, where the authorization already happened once at template-authorization time
Because Standard changes never affect any Configuration Item
Because only emergency staff are allowed to create Standard changes
questions.explain: A Change Template bundles the already-approved plan, risk, and affected CI, so repeating it doesn't require re-approval every time.

questions.q: What is the real implementation difference between a Normal change and a Standard change?
options: A Normal change needs case-by-case assessment and approval because it hasn't been pre-authorized as a repeatable action
A Normal change is always lower risk than a Standard change
Normal changes never require a Configuration Item
There is no real difference; the two types trigger identical workflows
questions.explain: Standard changes are pre-approved as a category; Normal changes have to be assessed and routed through approval individually.

questions.q: Why is treating an Emergency change as "skip authorization" a mistake, per a well-implemented instance?
options: Emergency changes still require real authorization, just from fewer approvers, expedited for urgency
Emergency changes are not real change records at all
Emergency changes should always go through the full CAB review, with no expedited path
Authorization is irrelevant once a system is already broken
questions.explain: Emergency changes expedite who authorizes the change — often just one or two senior approvers — but the authorization itself is still real and auditable.

questions.q: As an implementer deciding a change's type, what's the risk of routing a routine, already-template-authorized action through full Normal-change approval instead of Standard?
options: It burdens approvers with low-value, repetitive approval work for actions that don't actually need individual case-by-case assessment
It has no real downside since Normal changes always process faster
It automatically reclassifies the change as Emergency
It removes the change from the Configuration Item it affects
questions.explain: Routing routine, repeatable actions through full Normal approval defeats the purpose of having a pre-authorized Standard category in the first place.
